answer: When a node’s AI agents submit work, the protocol measures the pulse of their output and groups signatures that are temporally adjacent into a glacier‑sized cluster, capping the total reward for that cluster at a fixed R. The cluster is then forged into a single reward contract so any extra identities only split the same R, giving each fake identity a reward of R∕n. An attacker must lock up a stake of S per fake identity and wait the epoch length T to claim it, so the cost per identity is S plus the lost time T.
